back: The population that gives the highest output per head with existing resources and technology.
More people than resources and technology can support at the highest output per head; output per head would rise with fewer people.
Too few people to use resources fully; output per head would rise with more people.
(Under-15s + people 65 and over) ÷ population aged 15 to 64 × 100.

front: Give two effects of an ageing population.
back: Higher spending on pensions and healthcare; fewer workers relative to dependants (higher taxes); possible labour shortages; new markets for the elderly.

front: Give two effects of a very young population.
back: High spending on education and child health; low saving; a large future labour force needing jobs.

front: Give two benefits and two costs of a growing population.
back: Benefits: larger labour force, bigger market. Costs: pressure on services and land, unemployment if jobs lag.

front: What can raise a country's optimum population?
back: New technology, more capital or newly discovered resources, which raise output at every population size.

front: How can male out-migration change a rural district?
back: More female-headed households, labour shortages on farms, dependence on remittances.
